saints.name: St. Hunna
saints.title: Matron
saints.shortBlurb: A noblewoman of Alsace called “the Holy Washerwoman” for washing the clothes of the poor with her own hands…
biography: Hunna was a noblewoman of seventh-century Alsace, the daughter of a duke, who married Huno, a nobleman of Hunawihr. She raised her son under the guidance of St. Deodatus, the former bishop of Nevers then living as a hermit in the Vosges, who baptized the boy and gave him his own name.

Mistress of a great household, she spent herself on her poorer neighbors: she nursed the sick, taught the faith, and cooked, cleaned, and washed for those who had no one else. Because she carried home the dirty clothes of the poor and brought them back clean, the country people called her 'the Holy Washerwoman'.

She died about 679 at Hunawihr and was buried there; her son became a monk in Deodatus's monastery at Ebersheim and was himself venerated as a saint. Pope Leo X canonized her in 1520, when her relics were raised on 15 April, her feast day; and for the lowly service that was her glory she is invoked as patroness of laundresses.
saints.knownFor: Serving the poor by washing their clothes with her own hands.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 15 April
Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 15 April
